original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 4 total physical Core Count for each populated processor record, including use of the extended Core Count 2 field when required, matches the approved CPU topology and persists after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 records, bind sockets/status, interpret the legacy Core Count selector and extended Core Count 2 field correctly, compare total physical cores with the approved CPU SKU/topology and a scoped read-only OS correlation, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the per-socket physical-core baseline, extended-field and disabled-core policy, OS correlation scope and reboot plan. Core collection and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Expected total physical core count for each populated processor/socket
Applicable SMBIOS version and legacy Core Count versus Core Count 2 decoding policy
Approved distinction among total cores, enabled cores and logical threads
CPU SKU/socket mapping and any fused-off or project-specific topology allowance
Validated SMBIOS/OS topology tooling plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and OS topology queries; do not enable/disable cores, alter SMT, hotplug CPUs or modify firmware.
Preserve raw legacy and extended count fields with formatted length; a decoded line alone can hide incorrect sentinel use.
Do not compare total Core Count directly with OS logical CPU count or Enabled Core Count; document topology math and disabled-core policy.
Use OS topology only as corroboration under bare-metal/visibility assumptions, not as a substitute for the firmware field.
Stop on invalid selector/extended-field combinations, mapping ambiguity, unexplained drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete Type 4 raw/decoded data, resolve effective physical Core Count per socket, compare with SKU/topology and approved OS correlation before/after reboot.
Do not change core/SMT controls, invent a topology allowance or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve expected physical core counts, fused/disabled-core semantics and extended-field interpretation.
Approve OS correlation and reboot/recovery, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is relevant, but grep can also match Enabled Core Count, loses socket/raw-field context and cannot validate the legacy 8-bit selector against Core Count 2.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 4 records, calculate effective Core Count from the version/selector/extended field and correlate per socket with the approved physical topology.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Core Count scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the legacy Core Count byte and Core Count 2 according to formatted length and SMBIOS semantics, retain both raw values, bind them to populated sockets and compare total physical cores with the approved SKU/topology before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems, including processors exceeding the legacy one-byte count range.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, CPU SKU/topology, parser/dmidecode and OS versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Core Count and Core Count 2 semantics, processor/platform topology specification and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds extended-field selection, raw provenance and explicit separation from enabled cores and threads.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; prevents truncation/sentinel errors that a decoded grep can miss.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS-visible topology may exclude disabled/offline resources or be constrained by virtualization; discrepancies require layer-aware analysis.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve SKU-specific fused core counts or visible-topology correlation rules, but must keep total Core Count distinct from Enabled Core Count and Thread Count.
expected_evidence: Approved per-socket physical-core baseline, SMBIOS/version decode rule, disabled-core policy and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with socket/status, formatted length, raw legacy/extended fields and effective Core Count
Scoped read-only OS topology correlation with explicit core-versus-thread math
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with any SKU/fuse exception

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and criterion consistently target total Core Count; absent platform baseline and extended-field rules are execution inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Both legacy and extended fields can be read safely; missing expected topology does not make the review semantically indeterminate.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds socket identity, raw selector/extended-field validation and physical/enabled/logical separation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains useful physical-topology correlation while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE and separating engineer verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Covers Core Count 2 and rejects substring grep ambiguity with Enabled Core Count.

review_improvement: Prevents false validation of a truncated legacy field or accidental comparison with enabled cores/logical CPUs.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once the expected topology and decoding policy are approved, all core capture, effective-value computation, correlation and reboot persistence checks are software-controlled.
